p3.title: Clinical Synthesis & Key Findings
p3.sub: Non-SOAP format. Prepared from the supplied PosturePulse assessment and supplemental metric summaries.
p3.reviewed: 21/21 video-derived posture metrics; supplemental posture and bilateral thermal summaries
p3.synthesis: The supplied measurements show small static alignment differences, most evident in sagittal trunk inclination and side-specific landmark offsets. Several frontal-plane findings overlap their stated reference once measurement uncertainty is considered. The bilateral trapezius and lumbar thermal differences are 0.0 C in the supplemental summary, indicating no measured side-to-side thermal asymmetry at that capture. These data do not establish a structural disorder, pain generator, neurologic deficit, vascular abnormality, or diagnosis.

findings.label: Trunk position
findings.text: left and right trunk inclination were -2.9 +/- 2.4 deg and -4.0 +/- 2.3 deg relative to the source system's 0-degree reference. Their uncertainty intervals remain below 0 degrees, supporting a small measured inclination during this recording.

findings.label: Lateral translation
findings.text: lateral body shift was -1.2 +/- 1.0% of stature. Small in magnitude, but its stated interval does not cross the 0% reference.

findings.label: Frontal alignment
findings.text: head tilt, shoulder-line tilt, hip-line tilt and trunk lateral lean each overlapped the source reference after uncertainty was applied; no definite frontal-plane deviation can be inferred.

findings.label: Side-specific offsets
findings.text: left ear, shoulder and hip offsets were greater than corresponding right-side values. Geometric observations without source reference ranges; require correlation with stance, camera position and examination.

findings.label: Knees
findings.text: knee extension overlapped 0 degrees bilaterally. Knee frontal alignment was explicitly labeled a proxy, carried wide uncertainty, and had no source reference value.

findings.label: Thermal summary
findings.text: trapezius Delta T and lumbar Delta T were both +0.0 C against the supplied <0.5 C comparison criterion. Supports bilateral surface-temperature symmetry only under the conditions of that capture.

p3.integrity: The primary PDF reports raw landmark geometry and uncertainty. The supplemental posture table reports transformed values against a 90-degree 'ideal'. The definitions, processing version and uncertainty for those transformed metrics are not provided; treat as a separate summary layer, not substituted for or averaged with the primary PDF values.
p3.qualification: The labels 'textbook perfect', 'optimal neurovascular symmetry' and 'excellent' exceed what these measurements can establish. A 0.0 C side-to-side difference does not prove normal neurovascular function, and a single static posture value does not determine pathology or clinical risk.

p4.uncertainty: An uncertainty-overlap result means the measured interval includes the reference and should not be called definitively abnormal. For side-to-side differences, the source does not provide covariance or a validated minimum detectable change; arithmetic differences are descriptive only.

p5.title: Clinical Implications & Management Framework
p5.sub: Translates the measured pattern into a safe clinical workflow. Not a diagnosis or treatment prescription.
p5.significance: The pattern is best characterized as minor static postural asymmetry with small sagittal trunk inclination. Relevant frontal-plane uncertainty intervals overlap the source reference. Side-specific offsets may reflect stance, camera perspective, landmark localization, natural asymmetry or a reproducible strategy; significance depends on symptoms and repeatability. Equal bilateral trapezius and lumbar surface temperatures are neutral rather than diagnostic.

steps.rule: Record pain, aggravating tasks, neurologic symptoms, work exposure, tolerance and prior injury.
Assess relaxed stance/gait, regional motion, landmarks, strength, sensation, reflexes and relevant provocation.
Match camera setup, stance, clothing, lighting and software; obtain at least two trials.
If symptomatic, use position changes, ergonomic adjustment and graded mobility/strength work.
Prompt assessment for progressive deficit, gait change, bowel/bladder or saddle symptoms, severe night pain, fever, trauma or systemic illness.

p5.outcomes: Prioritize symptoms and task tolerance. Secondary outcomes are repeatable changes in trunk inclination and lateral shift beyond expected variability, supported by functional tests and standardized side-offset or thermal measurements.
p5.limitations: Single static video-derived observation; no direct assessment of bone, joint pathology, muscle activation or dynamic control. Several values are unreferenced proxies, not disease thresholds. The source is marked draft and not clinically validated. The supplemental posture convention lacks uncertainty and algorithm provenance; thermal data lack absolute temperatures and acquisition protocol.
p5.evidence: Photogrammetry can provide repeatable quantitative posture measurements when acquisition and landmarks are standardized, but validity varies by method and metric. Thermal measurement reliability likewise depends on equipment and protocol; symmetry alone is not a diagnosis.
p5.conclusion: The available evidence supports documenting a small, non-acute static alignment pattern and bilateral thermal symmetry at one time point. It does not support a diagnosis, a claim of neurovascular normality, or a universal posture correction target. Clinical decisions should be driven by symptoms, examination, function and standardized repeat measurement.
